title: Density-driven discrete transitions are rare in 1D CAs, common in higher dimensions

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Density-driven discrete transitions are rare in 1D CAs, common in higher dimensions

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Cellular automata in which a continuous change in initial density of black cells produces a discrete switch in long-time behavior, with whichever color was initially more common taking over the whole system, are fairly rare in one dimension, where domain boundaries often get stuck, but become increasingly common in two and more dimensions.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 7: Mechanisms in Programs and Nature

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And so long as the boundaries of the regions do not get stuck—as happens in many one-dimensional cellular automata—the result is that whichever color was initially more common eventually takes over the whole system.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 7, “Mechanisms in Programs and Nature”; section “Origins of Discreteness” (from p. 337), p. 339. Scope: cellular automata in one, two and more dimensions started from random initial conditions of varying density

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch07-14: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.81

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The transition and takeover behavior have direct computational criteria. Elementary and other bounded rule spaces can be exhaustively or systematically sampled using public software. The unrestricted comparison across all dimensions and rule parameterizations prevents a fully general resolution.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate specified one-, two-, and higher-dimensional binary cellular-automaton rule classes, initialize each over densities bracketing one half, and classify whether the majority color reaches consensus as size and time increase. Compare the fraction of qualifying rules by dimension and test boundary pinning as a mediator.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Increasingly common depends strongly on the sampled rule family and neighborhood.

Finite simulations can confuse very long transients with stuck boundaries.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.72
operationalizability: 0.82
analysis feasibility: 0.72
discriminating power: 0.85
data existence: 0.9

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The decision criterion is a discrete change in the absorbing state as initial density crosses one half, which is unambiguous for a finite lattice. Elementary one-dimensional rules can be enumerated completely, and a stratified sample of two-dimensional rules is a standard computation of days to weeks. That is enough to confirm or refute the stated dimensional comparison.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For one- and two-dimensional cellular automata drawn from stated rule classes, sweep the initial density of black cells and record whether the long-time density jumps from one absorbing color to the other near one half. The frequency of that jump, and of stuck domain walls, can then be compared across dimension. A rising frequency with dimension would support the claim; a flat or falling frequency would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fairly rare and increasingly common become numbers only after the rule ensemble is fixed.

Two- and higher-dimensional rule spaces must be sampled rather than exhaustively listed.

fields.value:
